subject: ela
intro: Nonfiction texts often explain how something happens, why it happens, or the steps in a process. As a reader, your job is to explain it back using the exact information in the text. Look for time-order words like first, next, then, and finally to follow steps. Look for cause words like because, so, and as a result to explain WHY something happened. A good explanation tells both what happened and the reason behind it, using facts from the passage.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Water is always on the move in a cycle. First, the Sun heats water in oceans and lakes, turning it into an invisible gas called vapor that rises into the air. Next, high in the sky, the vapor cools and forms tiny drops that make clouds. Finally, when the drops grow heavy, they fall back to Earth as rain or snow.

Using the text, explain what happens to water after the Sun heats it.

steps: I find the step that comes right after the Sun heats the water.
The text says the water turns "into an invisible gas called vapor that rises into the air."
Then that vapor cools and forms clouds, so I explain that order.
solution.answer: After the Sun heats the water, it turns into vapor that rises into the air. Next the vapor cools high in the sky and forms tiny drops that make clouds. The text says the vapor "cools and forms tiny drops that make clouds."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

In 1955 in Alabama, Rosa Parks rode home on a bus. At that time, unfair rules forced Black riders to give up their seats to white riders. When the driver told Rosa to move, she refused. She was arrested. Her brave act led thousands of people to protest the unfair bus rules, and the rules were finally changed.

Using the text, explain what happened after Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat, and why it mattered.

steps: I look for what happened next in the events.
The text says she "was arrested" and her act "led thousands of people to protest."
I explain both the event and its result, which was that the unfair rules changed.
solution.answer: After Rosa Parks refused, she was arrested. Her brave act led thousands of people to protest the unfair bus rules. This mattered because, as the text says, "the rules were finally changed."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Have you ever wondered why leaves turn red and orange in the fall? All summer, leaves are green because of a substance that helps the plant make food from sunlight. When days grow shorter and colder, the plant stops making food. The green fades away, and colors that were hidden all along finally show through.

Using the text, explain why leaves change color in the fall.

steps: I look for the cause of the color change.
The text says leaves are green because of a food-making substance.
When it gets "shorter and colder," the plant stops making food, the green fades, and hidden colors show.
solution.answer: Leaves change color because, as days grow shorter and colder, the plant stops making food. The green substance fades away, so the red and orange colors that were "hidden all along finally show through."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

To plant a bean seed, follow these steps. First, fill a small cup with damp soil. Next, poke a hole about one inch deep and drop in one bean. Then cover the bean gently with soil. Finally, place the cup near a sunny window and water it a little each day.

Using the text, explain the steps for planting a bean seed in order.

steps: I follow the time-order words: first, next, then, finally.
First fill a cup with damp soil, next poke a hole and drop in a bean.
Then cover it with soil, and finally put it in the sun and water it daily.
solution.answer: First, fill a small cup with damp soil. Next, poke a hole about one inch deep and drop in one bean. Then cover the bean gently with soil. Finally, place the cup near a sunny window and water it a little each day.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A caterpillar goes through amazing changes to become a butterfly. First, it eats leaves and grows quickly. Next, it forms a hard case called a chrysalis around its body. Inside, its body slowly changes shape. Finally, it breaks out as a butterfly with colorful wings.

Using the text, explain what a caterpillar does right after it stops eating leaves.

steps: I find the step after the caterpillar eats and grows.
The text says, "Next, it forms a hard case called a chrysalis around its body."
So that is what happens right after it stops eating.
solution.answer: Right after eating leaves, the caterpillar forms a hard case called a chrysalis around its body. The text says, "it forms a hard case called a chrysalis," and inside, its body slowly changes shape.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Long ago, a huge iceberg floated in the path of the ship Titanic. The lookouts spotted it too late. The ship could not turn in time, so it struck the ice. The crash tore a hole in the side, and water rushed in. Sadly, the great ship sank.

Using the text, explain why the Titanic sank.

steps: I look for the cause of the sinking.
The ship "could not turn in time, so it struck the ice."
The crash "tore a hole" and "water rushed in," which sank the ship.
solution.answer: The Titanic sank because it struck an iceberg that the lookouts spotted too late. The crash "tore a hole in the side, and water rushed in," which caused the ship to sink.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Why do we get hiccups? A large muscle under your lungs, called the diaphragm, helps you breathe. Sometimes it suddenly tightens when it should not, perhaps because you ate too fast. This quick tightening pulls in air, and the top of your throat snaps shut, making the sound "hic."

Using the text, explain what causes the "hic" sound of a hiccup.

steps: I trace the chain of causes.
The diaphragm "suddenly tightens," which "pulls in air."
Then "the top of your throat snaps shut," making the sound.
solution.answer: A hiccup happens when the diaphragm suddenly tightens and pulls in air. The "hic" sound comes because "the top of your throat snaps shut" as the air is pulled in.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

To make butter, start with a jar of heavy cream. First, pour the cream into the jar and screw the lid on tight. Next, shake the jar hard for about ten minutes. As you shake, tiny bits of fat begin to clump together. Finally, a lump of butter forms and separates from the watery liquid.

Using the text, explain the steps to make butter and what happens as you shake the jar.

steps: I follow the steps in order.
Pour cream in, close the lid, then shake hard for about ten minutes.
As you shake, "tiny bits of fat begin to clump together," and finally butter forms.
solution.answer: First, pour heavy cream into a jar and screw the lid on tight. Next, shake it hard for about ten minutes. As you shake, "tiny bits of fat begin to clump together." Finally, a lump of butter forms and separates from the watery liquid.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

In 1861, the United States split into two sides in a war. The Northern states wanted to keep the country together and end slavery. The Southern states wanted to keep slavery and form their own country. After four long years of fighting, the North won. As a result, slavery was ended across the whole nation.

Using the text, explain why the two sides went to war and what happened as a result.

steps: I find the reasons each side fought.
The North wanted to keep the country together and end slavery; the South wanted to keep slavery and form its own country.
The result was that the North won and "slavery was ended across the whole nation."
solution.answer: The two sides went to war because the North wanted to keep the country together and end slavery, while the South wanted to keep slavery and form its own country. As a result of the North winning, slavery "was ended across the whole nation."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Why does the Moon seem to change shape each night? The Moon does not make its own light. It shines because sunlight bounces off it. As the Moon travels around Earth, we see different amounts of its sunny side. When we see the whole sunny side, it looks like a full circle. When we see only a sliver, it looks like a thin curve.

Using the text, explain why the Moon appears to change shape. Include the cause.

steps: I find the real cause of the change.
The Moon "shines because sunlight bounces off it," and it travels around Earth.
We see "different amounts of its sunny side," which makes it look like it changes shape.
solution.answer: The Moon appears to change shape because it does not make its own light. It shines when sunlight bounces off it, and as it travels around Earth, "we see different amounts of its sunny side." Sometimes we see the whole sunny side and sometimes only a sliver, so it seems to change shape.
